gloss: to be transparent; to be see-through; to be obvious

definitions.gloss: to be transparent; to be obvious; to be see-through
definitions.explanation: Used figuratively to describe lies, intentions, or excuses that are so obvious they can be easily seen through.

examples.japanese: {見|み}え{透|す}いた{嘘|うそ}をつくな。
examples.english: Don't tell such an obvious lie.

examples.japanese: そんな{見|み}え{透|す}いたお{世辞|せじ}は{嬉|うれ}しくない。
examples.english: Such transparent flattery doesn't make me happy.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{見|み}え{透|す}いた{言|い}い{訳|わけ}に、{誰|だれ}も{騙|だま}されなかった。
examples.english: Nobody was fooled by his transparent excuse.

notes:
CONJUGATION: Godan く-verb. {見|み}え{透|す}く → {見|み}え{透|す}いて → {見|み}え{透|す}いた.

USAGE:
Almost always used in the past participle form {見|み}え{透|す}いた as a modifier: {見|み}え{透|す}いた{嘘|うそ} (an obvious lie), {見|み}え{透|す}いた{手|て} (a transparent ploy). Rarely used in other conjugated forms.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見|み}え{透|す}いた{嘘|うそ} (a transparent lie)
- {見|み}え{透|す}いた{手口|てぐち} (an obvious trick)
- {見|み}え{透|す}いたお{世辞|せじ} (obvious flattery)
